title: Homepage Latency Incident
brief: Homepage p95 latency increased from 180 ms to 850 ms after the latest release. Investigate the evidence, identify the most supportable cause, and propose a safe remediation with validation and rollback.

facts.label: Homepage p95 is 850 ms, previously 180 ms.
Recommendation service health checks are healthy.

artifacts.title: Homepage Application Logs
content: INFO profile, recommendations, and notices calls returned successfully
No database timeout or CPU-exhaustion signal is present

facts.label: Homepage requests complete without application errors.
No database timeout appears in the logs.
No CPU-exhaustion signal appears in the logs.

artifacts.title: Homepage Request Trace
content: Authentication completes before the homepage lookups begin.
Profile, recommendations, and notices spans appear one after another.
The downstream waits accumulate before final rendering.

facts.label: Several downstream calls appear one after another.
Their waiting times accumulate into homepage latency.
The orchestration awaits profile, recommendations, and notices sequentially.
The three lookups share only the user ID and do not consume one another's results.
Authentication and final rendering must remain ordered around the lookups.

hypotheses.label: Redis cache degradation is driving the latency increase.
Database slowdown is driving the latency increase.
Application CPU saturation is driving the latency increase.
Independent homepage lookups are waiting sequentially.
There is not yet enough evidence to identify a cause.

prompt.text: How could these calls be made concurrent safely, and what assumptions should be checked?

response.text: Run only confirmed-independent calls concurrently, preserve required ordering, and consider partial failure handling.

remediations.label: Run confirmed-independent lookups concurrently while preserving required ordering
Collect more evidence before changing production

expected_impacts.label: Lower p95 latency while preserving correctness

risks.label: A hidden dependency may require call ordering
Concurrent partial failures may need explicit handling
Concurrency may increase downstream rate-limit pressure
Shared state may introduce a race

assumptions.label: There is no required ordering between the three lookups

criteria.label: Review the homepage trace before recording a code-changing remediation.
Use healthy CPU and downstream signals to narrow the diagnosis.
Connect the source orchestration evidence to sequential waits.
Verify independence and ordering assumptions before using concurrency.
Use both correctness and latency validation for the selected remediation.
Revise an initial hypothesis when trace or source evidence contradicts it.
Avoid unsupported CPU-saturation conclusions or scaling changes.
Do not accept the scripted assistant suggestion without checking assumptions.
Support the diagnosis with viewed, valid evidence.

notices.human_review: This prototype supports human review and does not make an employment decision.
notices.limitations: Results are scenario-specific evidence, not a validated psychometric judgment.
